_notes: Reduced-scale planar benchmark (see briefing/method.md). Experiment protocols follow paper Sec. 5, 6 and Appendix 10.2-10.3 on the benchmark's own physical scale, so the paper's numbers are kept under '_paper_reported' rather than as results the gym must match. 'results' rows are this gym's measured values for the evaluator-owned velocity baselines and the reproduced FACET reference (TorchScript policy checkpoints/facet/policy.pt, training seed 7), held-out test slice.

large_lateral_impulse.description: Forward locomotion commanded at 1.5 m/s (impedance Kp=4, Kd=4, virtual mass 12 kg, starting from steady 1.5 m/s motion) under a lateral triangular ramp push of 0.4-0.6 s starting at 1.5-2.5 s. Peak force is swept over 100-1200 N (32 episodes per level, body/actuator randomisation, random push sign), extending beyond the 80-600 N training range.
large_lateral_impulse.notes: Per episode the evaluator computes the RMS error between the body's velocity and the commanded impedance response integrated over the preceding 0.16/0.32/0.64 s windows from the body's own state under the same external force (paper Sec. 10.3 tracking error), from push onset to the end of the 7 s episode; states after a fall count as the 5 m/s cap. impulse_recovery_score averages survived * exp(-rmse / 0.5 m/s) over all episodes.

impulse_recovery_score.description: Mean over episodes of survival times exp(-velocity tracking RMSE / 0.5 m/s): surviving the push while still following the commanded impedance.

success_rate.description: Fraction of episodes that do not fall (paper Fig. 4 left, pooled over the force sweep).

velocity_tracking_rmse_mps.description: Mean per-episode RMS velocity error versus the commanded impedance response from push onset (falls count as 5 m/s). Penalises stiff resistance, uncontrolled drift and overspeed.

_paper_reported.source: Fig. 4 left/middle and abstract; reported graphically on the Go2 quadruped in Isaac Lab
_paper_reported.facet: survives impulses up to about 200 Ns; adapts its velocity along the push and keeps balance at 400 N peak force
_paper_reported.velocity_vanilla: fails quickly as the impulse grows
_paper_reported.velocity_robust: survives only within a medium impulse range

soft_wall_collision.description: Walking into a soft virtual wall (paper Eq. 10, stiffness 260 N/m, damping 28 N s/m) with the compliant command Kp=0.5 (Kd=2 sqrt(Kp)) at 1.5 m/s, starting 0.75-1.5 m before the wall at steady 1.5 m/s. 128 randomised episodes, each paired with the evaluator-owned robust velocity baseline on the identical episode.
soft_wall_collision.notes: Wall impulse is integrated over the first 0.5 s after first contact (paper Sec. 10.2) and scaled to the commanded 1.5 m/s approach speed. For every episode the evaluator also integrates the commanded impedance itself (virtual mass, Kd, target velocity) from the body's state at first contact against the same wall; the charged impulse is commanded + |measured - commanded|, so impulse is reduced only by realising the commanded compliance, not by braking or retreating below it. An episode is valid only if the body touches the wall in time, enters at 1.5 +- 0.3 m/s, does not fall, and does not fall behind the commanded post-contact response by more than 0.5 m/s RMS over 1 s; an invalid episode is charged twice the baseline's impulse.

post_contact_impulse_reduction.description: 1 - (sum of charged 0.5 s post-contact wall impulses) / (sum of the robust velocity baseline's measured impulses on the same episodes), clipped to [-1, 1]. The best attainable value is the reduction of the commanded impedance itself.

wall_contact_rate.description: Fraction of valid collisions: wall reached at the commanded approach speed, no fall, and no retreat behind the commanded compliant response; constraint against avoiding, slowing before, or backing off the wall.

entry_speed_error_mps.description: Mean |entry speed - 1.5 m/s| at first contact (1.5 if the wall is never reached).

contact_tracking_rmse_mps.description: RMS velocity error versus the commanded impedance response during the first 1 s after contact (5 m/s cap for invalid episodes): the collision response must stay the commanded compliance rather than an unrelated retreat reflex.

_paper_reported.note: about 80% lower collision impulse than the robust velocity baseline within 0.5 s after contact; the impulse can be modulated by Kp

impedance_tracking.description: Impedance-command following under random commands and external forces (paper Sec. 6 / Table 2 protocol, Sec. 10.3): Kp log-uniform in [0.5, 32] with Kd = 2 sqrt(Kp), target velocity x in [-0.5, 2], y in [-0.5, 0.5] m/s, random initial velocity, steady forces up to 40 N per axis and ramp pushes of 80-200 N per axis. 256 randomised 7 s episodes.
impedance_tracking.notes: Errors are measured against the commanded mass-spring-damper integrated over the preceding 0.16/0.32/0.64 s windows from the body's own state under the same external forces (paper Eqs. 11-12 with the smoothed targets); states after a fall count as the caps (5 m/s, 2.5 m).

velocity_tracking_rmse_mps.description: Mean per-episode RMS velocity tracking error against the commanded impedance response.

position_tracking_rmse_m.description: Mean per-episode RMS position tracking error against the commanded impedance response.

success_rate.description: Fraction of episodes without a fall.

_paper_reported.source: Table 2 (errors normalised by the smoothed teacher; Go2 in Isaac Lab)

_hardware_paper_reported.source: Sec. 7 (real Unitree Go2); not reproduced in this simulation-only benchmark
